tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the project's purpose, architecture, and key components. This document provides the high-level context needed before diving into the code.
tour.languageLesson: Start with documentation to understand the project before diving into code.

tour.title: Application Entry Points
tour.description: The entry points bootstrap the application, importing core modules and starting the runtime. These files are the foundation of the dependency graph.
tour.languageLesson: Entry points import core modules and configure the runtime. Follow the import chain to understand initialization.

tour.title: Project Configuration
tour.description: Configuration files define build settings, dependencies, and deployment rules. Understanding these is essential for development and deployment.
tour.languageLesson: Config files control build settings, dependencies, and runtime behavior. Changes here affect the entire project.

tour.title: Infrastructure & CI/CD
tour.description: Container definitions and CI/CD pipelines automate building, testing, and deployment. These files define how the application reaches production.
tour.languageLesson: Dockerfiles and CI pipelines automate building, testing, and deployment to production.

tour.title: Backend Core
tour.description: The backend implements the API layer, business logic, and data processing. These files are the most-imported in the backend, indicating core functionality.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI with Pydantic models. Async endpoints handle document processing and translation via Cloudflare Workers.

tour.title: Frontend Core
tour.description: The frontend implements the user interface with React and Next.js. These files are the most-imported in the frontend, forming the UI foundation.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js with React and Tailwind CSS. Server-side rendering for fast initial load.

tour.title: Cloudflare Workers
tour.description: The proxy and API workers handle request routing, authentication, and edge computing. They sit between the frontend and backend services.
tour.languageLesson: Edge computing via Service Bindings. The proxy worker routes requests to the API worker without public HTTP.

tour.title: Documentation
tour.description: Project documentation covers architecture decisions, API contracts, and development guides. These resources help onboard new contributors.
tour.languageLesson: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) document key design choices. Read these before proposing changes.

tour.title: Data Schemas
tour.description: Database schemas and API definitions establish the data model. These contracts ensure consistency between backend services and clients.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma schema defines the database model. GraphQL types mirror the API surface.

tour.title: Testing Strategy
tour.description: Test files validate correctness across the stack. The test directory structure mirrors the source, making it easy to find tests for any component.
tour.languageLesson: Playwright for E2E, Vitest for unit tests. Run make test before pushing.
